plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase SPY to 30% and QQQ to 20% for greater broad index exposure.
Add CRWD to 10% as a quality tech holding within limits.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
This plan prioritizes stability and lower drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a realistic target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, focusing on broad market exposure and income. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Reduce leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to smaller allocations.
This maintains some leveraged exposure while reducing overall risk.
The plan balances growth potential with a focus on risk management.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month by reducing overall leverage and concentration. It blends broad index exposure with quality tech and a small, controlled amount of leveraged ETFs. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, aiming for consistent growth.

plan: Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Increase allocations to leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL, PLTU) to 6% each.
This strategy leans into higher-beta assets for aggressive growth.
Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage amplified risks.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month by significantly increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs. This approach amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing effects on leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is essential to manage the higher risk of substantial losses.

plan: Increase QQQI to 30% and SPY to 20% for steady monthly distributions and broad index exposure.
Sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, SOXL, MSFU, MUU, SPAL) to near zero.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth.
Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index funds. It aims for low drawdown and reliable monthly distributions. While prioritizing income, remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns. This is not a savings account.
